$comment: The fields `spec/compounds.json` does NOT carry, plus the row set iOS actually ships. Hand-maintained; `spec/compounds.json` is NOT — it is a byte-identical copy of the web's and must never be edited here. Together these two files are the only inputs to spec/generate-plotter-compounds.mjs.
$tmaxProvenance: Every `tmax` below is transcribed from PLOTTER_COMPOUNDS in the web's public/app.js:10736 — a table T-60 established is DEAD (the in-app plotter was removed; App() redirects 'plotter' to /cycle-plotter/, and nothing reads it). It is kept anyway because the LIVE source has no tmax at all: pk.js derives ka analytically as ln2/max(0.01, halfLife*0.25) and never names a tmax. Deleting these would leave CalculatorEngine.pkBuildEntries with no absorption input; inventing replacements would put a fabricated number on a dosing curve. Both are out of scope for T-60 and belong to T-42, which already records iOS's ka-by-bisection as a divergence from the web's formula. DO NOT treat these as spec-backed.
$defaultDoseProvenance: Also from the dead PLOTTER_COMPOUNDS. Read by NOTHING in the iOS app today (grep defaultDose: only this table). `defaultDoseUnit` records the unit the number was written in, so the generator can refuse a row whose default dose silently changed meaning when the unit was reconciled to the live table.
$orderComment: The order the picker shows, preserved EXACTLY as the pre-T-60 table had it so the reconciliation is a data change and not also a reordering. It also keeps PlotterCompound.all[0] == test-e, which CyclePlotterViewModel uses as its unknown-id fallback.

staleDefaultDoseUnit.tb500: dead table said mcg, live table says mg — 2000 mcg = 2 mg
staleDefaultDoseUnit.hgh: dead table said mcg, live table says IU — no exact conversion (needs a mg-per-IU potency), so the number is left alone rather than converted
staleDefaultDoseUnit.pt141: dead table said mcg, live table says mg — 1000 mcg = 1 mg
staleDefaultDoseUnit.mt2: dead table said mcg, live table says mg — 500 mcg = 0.5 mg

$staleComment: These four `defaultDose` numbers are expressed in the OLD (dead-table) unit and the row's `unit` is now the live one. They were NOT rescaled, for the same reason tmax was not touched: T-60 reconciles half-lives and units, it does not rewrite dosing numbers. Nothing reads defaultDose today so nothing is wrong on screen — but ANY code that starts reading it must convert these four first. The generator refuses to emit a mismatched row that is not listed here, so a new one cannot slip in unannounced.

extras.$comment: Rows iOS carries that the LIVE plotter has no entry for at all, so there is nothing to reconcile them to. Transcribed from the dead PLOTTER_COMPOUNDS verbatim, `cat` included — which is why their category reads 'Peptide' rather than a live-vocabulary one ('Growth'/'Other'). That is deliberate: the off-vocabulary category is the marker that says 'not spec-backed', and PlotterCompoundSpecTests asserts it. Removing them is a product decision, not a reconciliation; it belongs to T-32.

notCarried.$comment: Spec compounds iOS does NOT ship. Every one needs a tmax before CalculatorEngine.pkBuildEntries can draw it, and the live source has none — so adding them means sourcing a number, which is exactly what T-32 says it will not do casually: 'a compound is a HALF-LIFE and a tmax, and the web's own note refuses to invent them'. Listed here so `spec/compounds.json` growing a 32nd compound FAILS the generator instead of being silently ignored.
notCarried.test-a: T-32 — ESTER_TO_CID maps 'Testosterone Acetate' here; the seed refuses cleanly today.
notCarried.sustanon: T-32 — ESTER_TO_CID maps 'Sustanon 250' here; the seed refuses cleanly today.
notCarried.hcg: T-32 — the hcg calculator shows the levels CTA and PlotterSeed refuses it.
notCarried.methenolone-e: T-32 — STEROID_TO_CID set; the steroid calculator does not show the CTA, so latent.
notCarried.winstrol-o: T-32 — STEROID_TO_CID set; latent. See also T-94.
notCarried.pinealon: Never carried by iOS; not referenced by any calculator or seed map.
